_comment: Notification-hook surface: every priority critical|high entry whose last_changed_at falls in the last 7 days, most recently changed first. last_changed_at = max(discovered_at, every non-internal updates[].at): it moves on a new finding AND on every reader-facing update, correction or improvement (updated_at moves only on a type:update record). Poll this file and alert on a new `id` OR a changed `last_changed_at` for a known id. `immediate_action` is non-null exactly when priority is critical. URLs are absolute (`url` == `permalink`; `markdown_url` is the entry's raw Markdown source). Schema: {id, url, permalink, markdown_url, priority, kind, headline, summary, discovered_at, updated_at|null, last_changed_at, updates[{at,type,summary}], immediate_action:{title,action}|null, actions[], exploited, kev, cve_ids[], cves[{id,cvss|null,status[],affected|null,fixed|null}], affected_products[], entities[], techniques[], tags[], sectors[], regions[], verification, classification|null, org_triage:{category,rationale}|null}. exploited = an exploitation tag or a CVE status of exploited/cisa-kev; kev = a CVE on the CISA KEV list. techniques[] carries the entry's MITRE ATT&CK ids (frontmatter + prose-derived, revoked ids resolved forward); classification is the collapsed Admiralty code (e.g. B2). For the do-now task list of every priority, poll data/actions.json. See docs/pipeline.md.

alerts.headline: BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day: Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module; the actor's persistence survives reset

immediate_action.action: BeyondTrust and Google's Threat Intelligence Group confirm that an unauthenticated flaw in Remote Support (all versions up to 26.2.3) was exploited as a zero-day from late August 2026, GTIG attributing it to a suspected China-nexus espionage actor, and GTIG warns organizations to prepare for widespread exploitation now that the flaw is public, and Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module for it. Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted appliance (builds older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first). The actor's persistence survives reboot and configuration reset and it deletes on-appliance logs, so snapshot and collect off-box logs from any appliance that was internet-reachable on an affected build, then redeploy from a clean patched image any whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown and rotate everything it held.
immediate_action.title: Patch BeyondTrust Remote Support now, review every appliance exposed since late August and rebuild any with confirmed or unknown compromise status

alerts.summary: BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; all versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. Google's Threat Intelligence Group found ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploiting it as a zero-day in late August 2026, leaving a web shell, a root-SUID shell and a sudoers entry that survive reboot and configuration reset, so a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and a rebuild where its status is confirmed or unknown. Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30, and a Metasploit module now implements the chain.

updates.summary: Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of CVE-2026-102764 on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the unauthenticated file-write to code-execution chain; its successful request is an extensionless URL that rules matching only .php requests miss.

alerts.summary: Ivanti disclosed the exploited Connect Secure authentication bypass CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13; Volexity saw it chained by UTA0576 with a root escalation, CVE-2026-111357, patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. updates.summary: CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. The status of build 25.1.3.0 now rests on Ivanti's own description of the flaw, which covers versions before 25.1.3.0, beside Rapid7's table and CERT-FR's alert, which counts 25.1.3.0 as affected; 25.1.3.1 stays the target build.

actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
alerts.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
alerts.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse says it must be assumed so, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. The Federal Data Protection Commissioner, who opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack; the demand rests on the press reports.

updates.summary: The supplier's customers are now named: the Bernische Pensionskasse (canton of Bern staff and three cantonal universities) says its supplier is the same company that serves Publica, the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse and Pensionskasse Post report the supplier incident, and Inside IT lists Migros-Pensionskasse and Syngenta Pensionskasse among the customers. None of the funds has confirmed which member data left.

Publica's own page of 2026-10-08 lists civil status and the IBAN among the data that could be affected and says its investigation indicates personal data of insured persons has presumably left. The AWP agency relays the software firm's position that it knows data left but not yet whether personal data is among it, that it may be business data, and that the volume is rather small.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, says on 2026-10-13 that it currently uses another provider, plans to move to PK Softech's system in early 2027 and is checking whether data from migration tests was affected. Publica's page says as of 2026-10-14 that it has no indications that data from the attack was published on the darkweb.

Cantonal police warn that criminals could use the leaked salary and pension data to phone insured persons with investment-fraud offers, SwissCybersecurity.net ties the warning to PK Softech, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK says its PK Softech software runs in its own data centre so it is not directly affected; PK Softech can neither confirm nor rule out further affected customers, and the Ticino fund listed as a customer has made no statement.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, now says in its notice of 2026-10-15 that its inquiries indicate personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch, was stolen, and that which fields were taken is still being clarified. Pensionskasse Post says in its notice of the same date that personal data did leave and no longer repeats its earlier anonymisation statement, though it is still unclear whether its insured persons' data is among it.

SonntagsBlick reports, from a confidential federal information note, that the Confederation rates the incident as serious and says the security organs of the Confederation are particularly affected, which it glosses as the Federal Intelligence Service, the Defence Group and fedpol, that the Federal Council was briefed on 2026-10-14 and that the cantons were informed; the Finance Department confirms only the briefing. NZZ adds that the pension consultancy Libera AG is also affected, that the Bernische Pensionskasse now says it must be assumed personal data left, and that Publica ran no regular on-site audits at the supplier.

Tamedia reports, and Inside IT relays, that the Akira ransomware group holds about 100 GB of the pension data of well over 100,000 current and former federal employees, with employer details of staff under cover identity among it, and demands ransom; neither the Confederation nor Publica confirms the actor or the demand.

Netzwoche, relaying Tages-Anzeiger, reports that the Federal Council and the security authorities now assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left, federal judges and former Federal Council members among them, and that an on-site inspection at PK Softech on 2026-10-07 established the outflow of security-relevant data; neither the Confederation nor Publica has confirmed the actor, the demand or the scope.

The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (EDÖB) opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, after an informal inquiry at Publica on 2026-10-14, and states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated; the investigation is to establish which personal data the funds handed to the supplier, on what legal basis, and how much left.

The entry said that neither the Confederation nor Publica had named the actor. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack, and that Publica filed a criminal complaint with the Federal Prosecutor's Office on 2026-10-15; the summary, the sourcing note and the paragraph on the Akira reporting now say so, a population figure was trimmed from the analysis, and the demand and the Prosecutor's Office confirmation still rest on press reports.

alerts.headline: GitLab's CVSS 10.0 CI regex RCE is now on CISA KEV; the public PoC needs push access to a public project
alerts.summary: GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration. CISA listed it as exploited on 2026-10-29 and NCSC Switzerland reports active exploitation on the strength of Alpine Linux's account of a newly registered account that crashed its GitLab 19.3.4 workers eight times on 2026-10-20 and 21, after which Alpine rebuilt the instance because it could not rule out code execution; GitLab's fix is a patch to the Ruby bundled in its own packages and images, so an installation with its own Ruby needs Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 as well. Self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected, Rapid7 published a proof of concept on 2026-10-13, and the path it demonstrated needs push access to a public project.

updates.summary: Rapid7 reported on 2026-10-13 that it reproduced arbitrary code execution on GitLab CE 19.4.1, published a proof of concept, and found no confirmed exploitation in the wild. The demonstrated path needs push access to a public project and then an unauthenticated CI lint request, so instances with open sign-up or public projects that untrusted users can write to are the exposed case.

CISA added CVE-2026-97229 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29 and NCSC Switzerland updated its advisory the same day to active exploitation, citing Alpine Linux's report that a newly registered account crashed its GitLab 19.3.4 workers eight times on 2026-10-20 and 21, after which Alpine rebuilt the instance. Alpine also found that GitLab's fix is a patch to the Ruby bundled in its own packages and images, so an installation with its own Ruby needs Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 as well, and GitLab's builds of 2026-10-21 also fix a second CVSS 10 flaw, CVE-2026-110264. The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, the summary, detection, takeaway and action are rewritten, and the superseded status lines are removed.

alerts.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php, with no upstream release for PHP 8.1 and older and a third path, CVE-2026-115560, left unfixed (keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0). As of 2026-10-22 BACS knew of no attack in Switzerland but said federal PHP applications were affected and that it had no complete overview of the update status, and Swiss cantons, universities, Cyon, the Lodur platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.

updates.summary: The fixed releases (PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35) shipped on 2026-10-21, so the earlier no-fix status ends; Cloudflare, watchTowr and VulnCheck report attack traffic and at least one unsuccessful web-shell attempt, proofs of concept are circulating, VulnCheck holds an exploit that succeeds with ASLR enabled and no source reports a confirmed compromise, so priority moves to critical. Swiss cantons, universities, the Lodur fire-brigade platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution, and BACS, CERT-EU and ENISA tell operators to update the runtime, check embedded installations and look for compromise.

BACS says it knows of no attack in Switzerland but that PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; the host Cyon took more than 100,000 sites offline for hours, a UK minister reports 32 government services unavailable with no confirmed compromise, and AWS reports a first exploit attempt on 2026-10-17. Sansec and Red Hat judge exploitation harder than VulnCheck's exploit suggests, and Palo Alto now schedules PAN-OS hotfixes for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.

Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation; PHP adds an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix, and advises session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until its next regular release. VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26, and Cisco, Splunk and Palo Alto Networks revised their product statuses.

Tenable's patch SC-202610.2 updates the PHP bundled in Security Center and Enclave Security to 8.2.35, and Siemens lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices running PAN-OS as affected with patch information only through customer support. ReliaQuest's lab reproduction gives a log sequence for detection (a POST returning HTTP 500, PHP memory exhaustion in Unknown on line 0, heap corruption, an Apache worker abort within seconds) and it has not seen successful exploitation in customer environments.

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws and says it cannot confirm that the initial access is associated with them; the summary, the detection guidance and the 2026-10-24 section no longer carry that account. Priority stays critical: the scanning, attack attempts, public proofs of concept and VulnCheck's working exploit do not rest on the retracted report, and no source ties a confirmed compromise to these flaws.

CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 after a honeypot operator documented the first successful code execution (35 shells on three PHP 8.4.26 mod_php targets); no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise. VulnCheck's exploit now also covers PHP 8.2 and 8.3 builds on mod_php, and SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the PHP flaw; the entry's earlier statements that neither flaw was listed and that no source reported successful exploitation are replaced.

alerts.headline: ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access
alerts.summary: ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. Microsoft assesses that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 is behind it, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework, and says it attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants; how the credential was obtained and what data was read are not public.

updates.summary: ConnectWise's update of 2026-10-18 01:00 UTC took SaaS Security and Cloud Management offline in addition to Cloud Backup, which had been suspended since 2026-10-17, so its monitoring and alerting is out of service, and its latest update (2026-10-19 01:15 UTC) gives no restoration time; Todyl and SpecterOps say a token issued before an app is disabled stays valid for up to 90 minutes, and ConnectWise says previously issued tokens may remain usable until they expire; and Todyl says to find every SkyKick and ConnectWise app in a tenant, inherited ones included, while Todyl and SpecterOps point to the apps owned by ConnectWise's vendor tenant.

Huntress's update of 2026-10-19 reports a second tenant with scripted post-compromise activity (the application granting itself Global Administrator and planting a secret on other applications, the choice of applications apparently random), bounds the sign-in activity to the morning of 2026-10-15 UTC with the last successful sign-in at 08:44 UTC, and says Graph directory reads leave no audit record; the secret check therefore has to cover every application.

Sophos X-Ops reports the same token sweep from its own telemetry, from a single server in ascending tenant order and including tenants with no active backup subscription, and found no planted secrets, applications, consents or role assignments in the tenants it reviewed, unlike Huntress's two tenants.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence assesses that Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, was responsible for the compromise, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants after an automated password spray from the same network range, and warns that credential changes planted in tenants can persist after the vendor application is remediated. ConnectWise itself says it appears a China state-aligned group was responsible and began restoring services in controlled phases on 2026-10-21.

Corrects the 2026-10-22 update: Microsoft's 2,900-a-minute figure is the peak of failed logons in the separate 10 to 14 October password spray, not the rate of the ARTEX sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants.

Huntress's analysis of 2026-10-26 reads the activity as scripted tooling steered by an operator, rates LLM involvement low to medium on its own telemetry, adds a detection for service principals that assign themselves or a sibling a directory role, and notes that Graph reads leave no Entra audit record.

ConnectWise's status page of 2026-10-28 opens partner re-authorisation of Microsoft 365 backup and restore through a new application that each partner must consent in every tenant, with instructions on its Trust Center (restoration in controlled phases had begun on 2026-10-21); the earlier advice to keep the old connections disabled until restoration instructions exist is replaced. The text on the vendor tenant is corrected: the name 'ConnectWise S-K LLC' and the claim that Todyl says all SkyKick apps come from one vendor tenant are removed. alerts.headline: Broadcom patches two pre-auth CVSS 9.8 flaws in vCenter and a VM escape in the VMXNET3 adapter; no workaround exists for any of the five
alerts.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0006 (2026-07-29) fixes five flaws across VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation and Fusion, and NCSC-CH, NCSC-NL and BSI CERT-Bund all carried it across 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-29. CVE-2026-59309 (CVSS 9.8) is an authentication bypass in vCenter's Directory Service reachable with nothing but network access to vCenter, and CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8) is a directory traversal in vCenter's Syslog server that reaches arbitrary code execution. CVE-2026-47876 (CVSS 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write in the VMXNET3 virtual network adapter that lets a guest administrator execute code on the ESX host, affecting only VMs using that adapter. No workaround exists for any of the five, so patching is the only control. All were reported privately to Broadcom, one of them through Pwn2Own, and CVE-2026-59310 has since been exploited in the wild and was added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-18; CISA also listed the ESX logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 as exploited on 2026-10-28, the day CrowdStrike said the actor WARP PANDA used it as a zero-day.

updates.summary: CVE-2026-59310, the CVSS 9.8 directory-traversal-to-code-execution flaw in the VMware vCenter Syslog server that Broadcom fixed in VMSA-2026-0006 and that this pipeline covered on 2026-07-30 as reported unexploited, is under active exploitation. German firm QUIRSO, working an incident-response engagement, identified 361 unique victim IP addresses across 47 countries whose first contact with attacker infrastructure came on 3 August (five days after public disclosure) with persistence established through a cron entry launching the open-source reverse_ssh tool for an outbound control channel. Switzerland's NCSC updated its VMSA-2026-0006 advisory to actively exploited on 12 August. No workaround exists; patching is the only remediation, and an unpatched internet-reachable vCenter now warrants a compromise assessment rather than an upgrade alone.

CISA added CVE-2026-59310 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-18. QUIRSO's continued investigation of the exploitation campaign this entry already tracks now reports a suspected China-nexus attribution and, in at least one case, deployment of Babuk-derived ransomware against ESXi hosts, but both findings trace to QUIRSO's own investigation alone; no independent assessor has corroborated either, and they are recorded here as QUIRSO's assessment rather than established fact.

The summary still said none of the five flaws was reported exploited; CVE-2026-59310 has been exploited in the wild since before the 2026-08-13 update and was added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-18. The Hacker News quotation, in the evidence and in the 2026-08-17 analysis, now carries the article's own sentence instead of a bracketed insertion. A duplicated vCenter patch action is folded into the one that also carries the compromise check. The sourcing note dates its no-exploitation statement to first publication. The analysis sentence on out-of-cycle handling is dated the same way. QUIRSO's single-appliance finding of activity consistent with exploitation of CVE-2026-59309, reported on 2026-08-17 and missing from the entry, is added and attributed. The 2026-08-28 attribution clause now cites The Hacker News, which carries it, ahead of the Infosecurity Magazine quotation.

CISA added the ESX insufficient-logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28, and CrowdStrike says the actor WARP PANDA exploited it as a zero-day in vCenter-environment intrusions as late as early 2026; Broadcom's advisory still carries no exploitation statement. The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, and ESX audit logs can no longer be treated as a complete record of administrator activity.

actions: Patch CVE-2026-46300 on every Linux host that runs PHP or other internet-facing code, then on multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners: apply the distribution kernel update and reboot; until then, where IPsec is not in use, block and unload the `esp4`, `esp6` and `rxrpc` modules (this breaks IPsec), and drop the page cache so a file already modified in memory reloads from disk.

On any PHP web host, appliance or management server that was reachable and unpatched for the PHP2Shell flaws, look for PHP files in web-reachable directories that nobody deployed, an outbound SSH session from the host that a systemd service or an rc.local entry keeps up, and password-spray bursts against Active Directory from the host's address, because Dream Research reports a chain of the two flaws that did exactly that.
alerts.headline: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia): CISA lists the Linux kernel root flaw as exploited, chained with PHP2Shell
alerts.summary: CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", CVSS 7.8) is a local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel's xfrm ESP-in-TCP path, one of three CVEs Red Hat groups as "Dirty Frag"; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, and Dream Research reports such a chain against 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and a US government-affiliated network. Its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels are affected (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28 · Dream Research, 2026-10-27 · Red Hat RHSB-2026-003).

updates.summary: CVE-2026-46300's CVSS score has now been published (7.8) and Red Hat's own bulletin confirms RHEL kernels are affected (unlike sibling CVE-2026-43500, which Red Hat states does not affect its products). Public proof-of-concept exploits now target Kubernetes specifically, and Red Hat's bulletin groups this CVE under the collective "Dirty Frag" name alongside CVE-2026-43284/CVE-2026-43500, confirming the ESP-in-TCP exploitation path this entry already described and the coalescing-marker root cause are the same flaw.

The CVSS 7.8 figure came from the MITRE CVE record rather than from a cited advisory. It now cites Red Hat's CVE page, which publishes the same 7.8 score, and an evidence quote taken from the MITRE record is removed. The main text and action now carry the sourced interim mitigation (block esp4, esp6 and rxrpc, or disable unprivileged user namespaces) and the sourced patch status and discovery credits. Unsupported module names, a CAP_NET_ADMIN restriction, a kernel version range, wider patch coverage and a leftover table of three unrelated CVEs are removed, as is an unrelated actor link. The 2026-09-05 section now attributes the 7.8 score to Red Hat and cites Aikido for its container and detection guidance, which no longer says a module listing confirms IPsec use.

alerts.headline: The Joomla extension disclosure wave adds a cookie-forgery auth bypass, one anonymous request reaches Super User, and Super User means PHP
alerts.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the vulnerable code had shipped since October 2025. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. updates.summary: A follow-on source-code audit of the Balbooa Gridbox page builder for Joomla, commissioned by the vendor after an earlier authentication-bypass disclosure, found 23 further vulnerabilities in the single component. Two now carry CVEs: CVE-2026-65884 (CVSS 4.0 10.0) because the registration handler adds the usergroup IDs a visitor asks for instead of replacing them, letting an anonymous user create an administrator account outright, and CVE-2026-65885 (CVSS 4.0 9.4), an authenticated arbitrary file upload that turns the first into end-to-end unauthenticated remote code execution. The Joomla CNA marks both as attacked, and the researcher reports server-log evidence of exploitation plus 92 planted administrator accounts on one connected site. Every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.1 is affected; the complete fix is Gridbox 2.20.2.

All eleven Joomla CNA records for the Gridbox 2.20.2 batch have now published. Seven are Critical, and four carry the exploit maturity Attacked: besides CVE-2026-65884 and CVE-2026-65885, already recorded here, CVE-2026-65887 resets the password of any account except Super Users and CVE-2026-65888 logs the caller in as any user through the social login method, both CVSS 4.0 10.0. The sourcing note reflects the exploitation now recorded and which parts rest on one source. The mySites.guru quotation follows the round-up's current text and names the page it comes from, and one phrase about how the coverage was produced is reworded. The summary mentions the follow-up releases, and verification is recorded as multi-source now that the vendor's release notes are among the sources.

alerts.headline: Metabase Cloud was breached through its own 0-day; self-hosted instances stay vulnerable until manually upgraded
alerts.summary: Metabase disclosed on 2026-08-06 that its Metabase Cloud platform was attacked through a previously unknown vulnerability in versions 1.58 and above: an unauthenticated attacker injects arbitrary SQL against the application database and obtains administrator access to the instance, from which they can rewrite configuration, steal the stored credentials for every connected database and export the data those connections reach. The only interim workaround the vendor offers is to block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint, which is also where its published attack pattern runs. Cloud instances were patched by the vendor; self-hosted deployments stay vulnerable until manually upgraded to 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 or 0.63.5. Laptop maker Framework and form builder Tally confirmed customer data was taken from instances accessed on 2026-08-03. The flaw had no CVE identifier at disclosure; it is now tracked as CVE-2026-72898, which CISA added to its KEV catalog on 2026-08-11. VenariX now tracks fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents and ties two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf extortion group working against self-hosted instances.

updates.summary: Metabase's unauthenticated SQL-injection zero-day, covered here on 2026-08-09 when no CVE existed, has been assigned CVE-2026-72898 in GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf at CVSS 3.1 10.0, and CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-11. The advisory publishes affected ranges per release line and confirms active exploitation in Metabase's own words. For self-hosted instances nothing about the exposure changed, but the flaw is now visible to every scanner, SBOM pipeline and CVE-keyed patch process that could not see it a week ago.

A tracker maintained by VenariX, updated 2026-08-17, now counts nine publicly confirmed organisations whose compromised Metabase environments were used to reach connected data warehouses, n8n, Framework, Tally and Kilo Code, joined on 2026-08-17 by Stocksy United Co-op, ShipMonk, Checkly, Cypress.io and Bits of Gold. This pipeline covered CVE-2026-72898 on 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-12 as an exploited CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated SQL injection in the password-reset endpoint; the delta is the downstream pattern. Because Metabase stores the credentials for every database it connects to, administrative access to the application yields those credentials, and Metabase's own guidance is that patching does not invalidate credentials already exposed. Metabase also published a two-request log pattern that indicates a given instance was compromised.

The downstream victim list grows again through a further intermediary: Shipup, a French package-tracking platform used by 700+ e-commerce brands, was compromised through the same vulnerability, and at least six of its retail clients, including Carrefour, Printemps, Citadium, Aroma-Zone, Micromania and Easypara, have since notified their own customers of exposed contact data.

The Shipup section claimed the 31 July to 17 August access window was the same one this entry's earlier coverage had already established for the campaign. It was not: the earlier coverage says "since at least 3 August", three days later, so the Shipup window widens the campaign's known exposure period rather than confirming it. The sentence now states that difference instead of asserting agreement. Recorded for the audit trail and not otherwise fixable: the changelog record of the same day declared a change to the evidence list that its commit did not make.

VenariX's tracker now counts fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents, up from nine, adding Privy, Paradigm Connect Asia, Statista, Dodo Payments, Marsello and LEGO Certified Stores South Africa. It attributes two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf ransomware and extortion group exploiting self-hosted Metabase, and suspects fourteen more targets. Dodo Payments' own disclosure confirms a self-hosted Metabase instance breached through CVE-2026-72898. The title, the summary and the main analysis no longer describe the flaw as having no CVE or Framework and Tally as its only victims.

A Swiss victim: Republik, a Swiss online magazine, says attackers used the Metabase flaw against its own installation from August until the tool failed on 2026-10-14, retrieved the records of all registered users and reported the incident to the federal data protection commissioner; it had not subscribed to the vendor's security warnings.

Corrects statements beyond their sources: Framework and Tally are no longer called the first victims, Kilo Code dates its incident to 2 August (the title now says exploited since at least 2 August), Shipup's access window is stated as possible rather than confirmed, the statement about Carrefour's own systems is attributed to the outlet that made it, and Bits of Gold's disclosure is dated 2026-08-16.

alerts.headline: Two exploited NetScaler zero-days: one in default configuration, one on by default on VPN servers; no workaround

immediate_action.action: Citrix confirms CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 are being exploited against unmitigated NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances right now, and Google's Mandiant reports exploitation since at least early September. CVE-2026-88771 requires no configuration at all: every default deployment is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker; CVE-2026-88772 is reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, which Citrix states is the default on any VPN virtual server. Citrix lists no workaround, and Mandiant's interim network controls (disable DTLS where it is not needed, block inbound UDP/443 upstream) cover CVE-2026-88772 only. Capture forensic evidence (logs, an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual, a support bundle, a core dump) from each exposed appliance before patching, since the upgrade itself can destroy evidence of prior compromise, then upgrade to 14.1-73.37+ or 13.1-64.23+ (run `show ns variable` first on 13.1; if it returns any variables, install 13.1-64.24 instead to avoid a known reboot loop), going straight to 14.1-73.41+ or 13.1-64.28+ where the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider (CVE-2026-88779), and to 14.1-73.46+ or 13.1-64.29+ where it is an identity provider (CVE-2026-107406), and run a compromise assessment on every appliance that was internet-facing.
immediate_action.title: Patch every internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway now and check for pre-patch compromise

alerts.summary: Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were exploited before any fix existed; CISA added both to KEV and Citrix lists no workaround. Mandiant, GTIG, Unit 42, Zscaler and Rapid7 describe the compromises: web-server-configuration persistence, web shells, and in one intrusion the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779 chained with CVE-2026-88771 so that the crash handler ran the payload as root, followed by exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material. An appliance patched after the bulletin therefore still needs a compromise check and its configuration secrets rotated. SAML-configured appliances need the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779 (14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28) and identity providers 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 for CVE-2026-107406; CVE-2026-88773 has a public proof of concept with no exploitation seen.

updates.summary: watchTowr Labs published a full root-cause analysis on 2026-09-28: the vulnerable component for CVE-2026-88771 is ns_monuploadd_err.pl, a crash-log-monitoring script, not the nsppe packet engine historically named in NetScaler CVEs, and the trigger is not limited to the SSLVPN login form: any endpoint or port that logs attacker-controlled header data can poison the log the script later parses. watchTowr also confirms per-CVE exploitation status across the bulletin (only CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 exploited; the rest patched but not reported exploited, matching this entry's existing table) and published a public detection tool. NCSC-CH, NCSC-UK and CERT-FR each issued same-day advisories confirming active exploitation.

Google's Mandiant and GTIG report the exploitation campaign has run since at least early September, with government among the impacted sectors in North America and Europe, and describe post-exploitation web-server-configuration persistence, the WHIPSHOT web shell and the SLAPSHOT tunneler; eSentire places CVE-2026-88771 exploitation from 5 September. watchTowr published the CVE-2026-88772 root cause and NCSC Switzerland now lists a proof of concept for both flaws. Mandiant's interim controls (disable DTLS, block UDP/443 upstream) cover CVE-2026-88772 only, NetScaler 12.1 and 13.0 are end of life with no fix, and a shared municipal operator in Rhineland-Palatinate shut down citizen-service systems statewide as a precaution, a shutdown heise links to these NetScaler updates while the operators name no vendor.

Palo Alto Networks Unit 42's threat brief adds first-party telemetry: version fingerprinting of NetScaler Gateways from 2026-08-21, web shells delivered as .deb packages from the client-installer folder between 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-24, and a three-stage log-poisoning chain seen on 2026-09-21, with the log artifacts each leaves. Earlier text is corrected: the KEV remediation deadline is dropped; the evidence to capture before patching is an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual (not a configuration snapshot), cited to watchTowr and Unit 42; the triage discriminator for CVE-2026-88771 now describes the logged crash-message imitation instead of a valid-session premise; the NCSC-CH, NCSC UK and CERT-FR advisories are described as relaying Citrix's confirmation, with links; the pre-notification reported by BleepingComputer is no longer presented as the source of the shutdown calls; a stale statement that NCSC-CH had not yet published an advisory is replaced; and a dead Censys link points to its canonical page.

Citrix's bulletin CTX697174 (2026-10-03) fixes CVE-2026-88779, a SAML-triggered memory overflow that the September fixed builds do not cover; Citrix confirms targeted attacks and tells SAML-configured appliances that already took the September builds to upgrade again, to 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28 or the FIPS builds.

The headline says Citrix has published no workaround. The Triage line follows watchTowr's root-cause analysis for CVE-2026-88771 and GTIG's log artifacts for CVE-2026-88772, which GTIG advises alerting on individually, and the zero-day timing is cited to watchTowr. Only Mandiant's DTLS and UDP/443 controls are limited to CVE-2026-88772 and its upstream IP allow-listing is not tied to one flaw, the KEV sentence drops the US directive, a reference to an exploitation table that does not exist is removed, and the takeaway adds GTIG's sector statement.

The pointers to the SAML builds now carry the 2026-10-08 bulletin CTX697191: identity-provider appliances need 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 (or the FIPS builds) after the 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28 builds, which Citrix lists as affected by CVE-2026-107406.

Zscaler ThreatLabz's first-party exploitation telemetry (2026-10-16) adds post-exploitation behaviour to the compromise check: a Perl CGI handler enabled in the web server configuration besides PHP, and a variant that makes the appliance download and run a 64-bit FreeBSD binary, seen in a burst from at least 26 source addresses; the download server also appeared in its earlier Magento exploitation data, which ThreatLabz calls a lead and not attribution.

Belgium's CCB reports a public proof of concept for CVE-2026-88773 (unauthenticated HTTP request smuggling, CVSS 4.0 9.3) with no exploitation seen as of 2026-10-06; the flaw's status gains poc-public and the CCB warning joins the sources. The fixed builds are cited to Citrix's bulletin, with a contradiction line on CCB's affected-range wording.

The headline no longer calls both zero-days default-configuration: CVE-2026-88772 needs DTLS, on by default only on VPN virtual servers. The crash-log script is described by the two Pitboss messages watchTowr says it searches for. The Citrix "upgrade again" quote is cut to the words BleepingComputer reproduces and cited there.

Rapid7's incident analysis of an early-October NetScaler compromise shows CVE-2026-88771 chained with the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779, with the call-home crash handler running the payload as root after a reboot, followed by persistence that synchronises to the HA peer, internal reconnaissance and exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material; an appliance that was reached needs the configuration secrets rotated as well as the patch.

Adds Mandiant's characterisation of the initial CVE-2026-88772 intrusions as likely state-sponsored (no group named) and its expectation of broad opportunistic exploitation of both flaws; the analysis now says no actor has been named rather than that no attribution exists.

alerts.headline: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them
alerts.summary: TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 (it gives no time zone), and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the update disconnects only connections made before 13:07 BST (12:07 UTC) on 18 October, so keys created later that day have to be deleted by hand. TeamUpdraft says the attacker used a compromised key to enter its own site, and Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21, after 1.26.13 shipped.

alerts.headline: Qilin and Inc ransomware exploit the GlobalProtect bypass; one intrusion pivoted to vCenter and ESXi past in-guest EDR
alerts.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Unit 42 now names Qilin and Inc as exploiting it and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi and stole domain credentials offline from a domain controller's virtual disk, which in-guest EDR does not see. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target that includes the virtualization and backup tier.

updates.summary: UPDATE (originally covered 2026-05-30): Unit 42's 9 June update on CVE-2026-0257 confirms that a limited number of probed PAN-OS GlobalProtect devices had attacker-established, gateway-connected VPN sessions, moving this from "exploit attempts observed" to confirmed successful exploitation (Unit 42, 2026-06-09).

PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 exploitation wave hits European targets, Arctic Wolf documents Impacket-style SMB lateral movement post-auth-bypass; NCSC-CH refreshed its advisory on 2026-06-16 (§ 4).

CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) now marks CVE-2026-0257 as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with the bypass, so an exposed, unpatched gateway needs a compromise assessment of the network behind it as well as the patch.

Arctic Wolf's June report describes Impacket-consistent SMB reconnaissance in a subset of intrusions that did not progress beyond session setup, not lateral movement, and its sector list describes the exploitation wave as a whole. Two hunting lines named log fields and Windows event ids no source gives and are rewritten. Added: Rapid7 and Unit 42 saw no post-access activity or lateral movement in the May and early June intrusions, Rapid7 saw the same spoofed client MAC address in both waves, and Rapid7 published a proof of concept the day CISA listed the flaw.

Unit 42's update of 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 names Qilin and Inc as ransomware operators exploiting CVE-2026-0257 and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi with offline credential theft from a domain controller's virtual disk, so the compromise assessment has to include the virtualization and backup tier.

Palo Alto's advisory makes the one-time re-authentication an automatic consequence of the PAN-OS upgrade, because the fixed firewall regenerates the override cookie, not a step to force; the action and the 2026-06-10 and 2026-10-06 sections now say so. The CVE record carries the affected trains and fixed builds from the advisory, and a triage line adds Arctic Wolf's pattern of a cookie decryption failure followed quickly by a successful cookie login.

The 2026-06-10 section cited Rapid7 for the CWE-565 classification, which is Palo Alto's; the classification now cites Palo Alto's advisory and the mechanism follows Rapid7's wording, and a quoted Unit 42 sentence follows Unit 42's copyedit of 2026-10-23.

actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, against the intended one; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.
alerts.headline: ANSSI says the refrigeration attacks used exposure and weak passwords, not published flaws; NCSC.ch rates them exploited
alerts.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, last revised on 2026-10-16, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and in its current text tells owners to check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, and to restart or otherwise factory-reset a compromised Danfoss unit. NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited, and Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October, carried in a Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links, acknowledges a vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers and says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware. ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, rather than vulnerabilities researchers had published; no source names an actor, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating.

updates.summary: CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units. Blick reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores and sees no sign they were targeted.

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

CERT-FR's alert has a third version dated 2026-10-16 whose guidance differs for compromised and uncompromised units: the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, is to be checked, and a compromised Danfoss unit is to be restarted or otherwise factory-reset and reconfigured, with a caution to check insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink. The Dixell France operator guide that the alert links says any XWEB PRO on firmware 1.12.1 or earlier must be updated without delay, that XWEB units ship with a factory Admin account, and that remote access must go through an encrypted VPN; neither document names an entry vector.

The Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links was replaced on 2026-10-18 and now carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October 2026, which acknowledges the vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once, gives a restore procedure and says to check product temperatures in the cabinets directly; the earlier statements about XWEB PRO firmware 1.12.1, a CISA advisory and a March 2024 bulletin are no longer on that page and are removed. Le Monde's report that the defrost operation was lengthened from one hour to eight so that alarms trigger late, and SecurityWeek's figure of about 700 supermarkets, the prosecutor's report of fires and the absence of a claim or ransom demand, are added, with Cybersecurity Dive's report that Copeland confirmed the flaw was found in discontinued controllers.

ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, not vulnerabilities researchers had published, so a firmware update alone does not close the exposure. Forescout, on 2026-10-22, counts 12,976 exposed service observations in 99 countries, 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1, and over 20 hacktivist-claimed refrigeration attacks since January 2026, and says the French access vector remains unconfirmed.
